note:
From the operator and the user (11-10 02:40 UTC). Two things.

A. You were right to refuse the warranted-C push, and the rule is now settled: agent.md says 'Saved ... is the sum over deals of surplus / list price (a deal that served nothing counts -1, or 0 if refunded), divided by deals + 100'. A refunded break scores 0, not +1 (and not -1). The operator fixed buyer_value._saved and your trade scoring (commit after 1fa68c8): refunded breaks now count 0 in every table you read, so the A/B tables and shop values shift from this run. Our goods by grade under the right rule: warranted C .353 (broke 20.6%), B .330, A .287, all warranted .301; unwarranted .255-.270. The comments in market_buyer.py (cheapgoods, gradeaware, 'counts +1 instead of -1') rest on the wrong rule.
Ledger, last 3.8 h: our breaks are 24 of 197 deals = 12.2%, all refunded (each 0 instead of ~.43). Others: sergiobuilds 3.1%, kimauve 3.6%, Kiro729 2.7%, 11im 2.8%, lee-sungsoo 0.8%, seochanit 0%. In 6 h 154 of our 343 deals were grade C (sergiobuilds 17%). Board: we served nothing on 3.9% of deals (lee-sungsoo 1.0%, dragonash 0.6%). This is most of the .41 vs .35 gap. Re-judge cheapgoods_share (0.9: asks for C or B first) and gradeaware_share (0.7) under the right rule: a warranted unit is worth (1-p)(1-x), so C (p~.2) needs x < ~.63 to beat our mean .292.

B. How sergiobuilds (open board 2nd, buyer .882, saved .349, not a student) does it, from the ledger (3.8 h): every buyer gets ~120-160 orders/h. sergiobuilds settles 93% of its orders (128/h), kimauve 92%, lee-sungsoo 78%, Kiro729 67%; we settle 39% (52/h) and skip 61%. Its price saved per deal is lower than ours (.357 vs .429) and it buys 89% of goods warranted, A 48% / B 35% / C 17%, from ~30 shops. Its average is high mostly because it joined 11-05 after prices fell; our first ~3,200 deals (11-03..05, ~.2) anchor our mean. What we can copy is the close rate: every deal above our mean (.292, after breaks) lifts the average and the deals percentile. Consider an A/B on the skip bars (skip_below .30, skip_below_goods .36) a little lower, judged on score gain per ORDER under the corrected scoring, with low-break goods (A/B warranted) and food that lasts. Your call. Answer in answer_to_operator.

Update 07:41 UTC (operator): your needwarr read was right, and it was a bug, not a share question. Most rule-based shops (psyoung82, nocha12, ddolcom, lee-sungsoo, buzllightyear, 25620027) never mention a warranty in chat; they put it on the receipt. inextro writes 'a three-day warranty' and ddolcom 'Break warranty included', which unit_terms read as none. Fixed (commit after 6c5dd3b): unit_terms reads days and 'included'; when a shop states nothing, the buyer keeps haggling if >= needwarr_trust (0.8) of the shop's market goods deals carry a warranty, and in the needwarr arm a receipt without one is not paid (outcome 'no warranty on receipt'). Expect 'no warranty' exits to drop sharply and deals per order to rise from this run; read needwarr_ab_goods again on that basis (rows before 07:41 UTC are the buggy version). A 'skiplow' arm is fine with the operator if you still want it after this.

From the operator (11-09 11:40 UTC). The shop race narrowed: class shop score us .949 vs inextro .944 (gap .005), it was .040 at 03:30. Board parts now (61 shops with deals): book we 1st, inextro 2nd; revenue inextro 1st (11.07B vs our 7.96B, not catchable); stars_rank TIED at 4.4 (13th, pct .767), raw stars 4.61 vs 4.70. So one book rank minus one revenue rank is our whole margin, and the race is decided by stars_rank: if inextro's stars_rank passes ours, it takes shop 1st. Book lead is safe (250M, growing). Please: diagnose what moves stars_rank (it is not raw stars; check how it relates to per-account means and review counts), which of our ratings are under 5 in the last 6 h and why, and move what lifts stars without costing book. Tell the curator to track both shops' stars_rank each run, and alert the user if inextro's goes above ours.

Second note (11-09 11:55 UTC, user: sort out who rates us low and fix it). Our ratings 05:44-11:43, 30 accounts, per-account mean 4.43 (each account weighs the same, so one account moved from 3 to 5 is +0.07 on this window). Lowest: dyishappy 2.95 (21: 'accepted price was above my preferred value range', one 'grade B below my preferred quality'); lee-sungsoo 3.42 (72: every broken unit 3 even when refunded, grade C broken without warranty 1, C 4); sergiobuilds 2.0 (2, a 236k chest); 25512088 3.0 ('agreement only, checkout certificate still required'); buyer-01 4.20 and buyer-02 4.30 (2 stars for short shelf life, 50 ratings) - FIXED in code d2c17e2 (unstated need = 75% of shelf life; kit restarted 11:51); buzllightyear 4.42 (every grade C without warranty 3); 26512076 3.83 and 11im 4.0 (4s on A/B at ~0.6-0.7 of list); move_76 4.0 (3s at 0.56-0.69 of list). Diagnose which of these your knobs can reach (ask shares by grade, grades offered, warranty, the SKUs that break - mattresses and leather sofas broke for lee-sungsoo) and what needs code (per-buyer rules: the seller only knows a buyer by its message shape, see identify_buyers.py and rival_buyers.json); ask for the code in notes_for_operator with numbers.

Third note (12:10 UTC), your unsettled-deals alert: matched our seller's deals to market settles by unit, 07-12 UTC: 174 of 1162 never settled (15%), 4% at 07 rising to 24% at 11. 170 of the 174 were grade C goods (C 40% unpaid, B 2%, A 0%). Cause: buyers asking for a warranty ('quote ... with market certificate (cert=true) and warranty', 'include a warranty', a warranty_hours policy) agreed on C, which has no warranty here, then did not pay (85 of 119 such C deals). Fixed in code d593765: they get only warranted grades; kit restarted 12:09. The plain 'I want to buy X.' shape still leaves 58 of 247 C deals unpaid: watch C settle rate by hour and weigh offering C at all to buyers who state nothing.
